discussion_comments.comment_body:
I assume you're trying not to re-export `Callable`. I would either not bother with the leading underscore of the import or put it in a `if typing.TYPE_CHECKING` block. But if this module isn't typed then you shouldn't introduce typing; only select modules in the stdlib have types.

As well, there's now a [`type` keyword for defining new types](https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html#whatsnew312-pep695) as of Python 3.12. Since this is an private module anyway, explicit exporting might now even be necessary.

I also think this name is misleading as it handles the execution of the statement, not just doing something pre-execution. So either this shouldn't do the execution and instead return something to print or nothing, or it should be renamed to something like `execution_hook`. And it might also make sense to be clear if this is for the entire statement or per line in the REPL (i.e., your example didn't show what happens when there are multiple lines).
